QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_1

question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil (CA and empanelled SIA) is reviewing the project design documents of Pragati Foundation, an NPO listed on NSE-SSE under the 'promoting education' eligible activity. The documents include a Logical Framework Analysis (LFA). For the SIA, what is the PRIMARY purpose of the LFA during her scoping exercise?

answer.text: To provide the basis for calculating the SROI ratio required under SAS-1400
To list the donors and the donations received during the financial year
To replace the statutory audit under Section 12AB of the Income Tax Act

To provide a structured tool that breaks the project into clearly defined components linking inputs, activities, outputs, outcomes and impact so the project can be planned, implemented, monitored and evaluated coherently

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 4.1, LFA is a systematic and structured tool widely used for project planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation. It breaks projects into clearly defined components (inputs -> activities -> outputs -> outcomes -> impact), ensuring clarity, coherence and accountability. For the SIA, the LFA is the read-off document against which the Annual Impact Report (AIR) is tested. **The Trap:** A confuses LFA with SROI computation (SROI is one downstream output). C confuses LFA (a design tool) with statutory tax audit (12AB registration renewal). B describes a donor register, not LFA. **Cross-Exam Context:** Tested conceptually in parallel with SAS-100 assurance framework (XXIII Ch 7) and cross-references V-B MF Foundation (which introduces project framing) and X-A/B Investment Adviser (CSR project due diligence). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Ask the SE for the LFA first — before AIR drafts, before KPI sheets. Without a defensible LFA, you cannot trace any indicator back to an objective, and your assurance report becomes a compilation exercise rather than an assessment.
